applicabilityBasis.summary: wARS is marketed for payments and transfers at a 1:1 Argentine-peso value, and the wFIAT product page describes minting, burning and fiat redemption. The official October 2025 wFIAT whitepaper identifies the exact wARS contract but denies any holder claim against the issuer and any redemption right. These primary disclosures conflict on the issuer-conversion-obligation requirement in GENIUS Act section 2(22), so applicability remains unclear.

genius.notes: As of 2026-10-07, no public token-specific GENIUS PPSI approval, official application, state qualification, OCC foreign-issuer registration, Treasury comparability determination or GENIUS enforcement action was located in the reviewed sources and regulator-domain searches. The current wFIAT whitepaper names only an unspecified Ripio group affiliate as issuer. Argentina wallet terms identify Moonbird S.R.L. as the service operator, and the June 30 reserve certificate leaves the issuing entity unnamed. The previous issuerEntity, Moonbird S.R.L. (Ripio), and its derivative domicile and licensing fields are removed because the reopened sources do not establish the exact token issuer. Payment applicability is unclear because marketing promises fiat redemption while the exact-token whitepaper denies a holder redemption right. No binding issuer redemption policy or monthly attestation series was established; reserve certification is publicly present and is expressly neither an audit nor a review. Primary issuer implementation remains proposed; the SCRC procedural rule does not establish issuer approval or make the Act effective. The DASP field records the pre-effective GENIUS posture only.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: As of 2026-10-07, no public token-specific PPSI approval, official GENIUS application, state-qualified approval, OCC foreign-issuer registration, Treasury foreign comparability determination or GENIUS enforcement action was located for wARS / Ripio, including the previously attributed Moonbird S.R.L.. The reviewed primary issuer-implementation materials are proposals. The September 30 SCRC procedural rule does not approve an issuer. This bounded negative-evidence review does not prove that no private filing exists.
